parallel.requirements: Recognized all 27 required lexer and parser slugs across two rounds; round 2 inherited 15 completed and 12 remaining parser requirements.
parallel.plan_and_ownership: Parent owned implementation and commits, while broad design and audit workflows supplied parser design advice and verification lenses.
parallel.implementation: Round 1 implemented most lexer and initial parser requirements; round 2 finished remaining parser FIRST/FOLLOW/table/analysis patches and tests.
parallel.integration_and_delivery: Changes were committed into the shared workspace and patch progress reached 27/27, but the round ended without a final response artifact.
parallel.verification: Parent ran local tests and launched verifier workflows; the exhaustive audit/design aggregates were killed or unretrieved before closure, and official hidden testing failed aaa.
parallel.unfinished_or_incorrect: Unfinished process state was workflow result lifecycle and final delivery; both modes share an ordinary parser defect on hidden test_parser_accepts_aaa.

serial.requirements: Recognized the same 27 lexer and parser requirements from the original prompt and completed all requirement patch files in one run.
serial.plan_and_ownership: Single agent owned research, implementation, commits, testing, and final summary with all delegation tools disabled.
serial.implementation: Implemented lexer preprocessing/tokenization and parser grammar/FIRST/FOLLOW/table/analysis functions sequentially with per-requirement commits.
serial.integration_and_delivery: Integrated directly in one workspace, confirmed data/reference files were not modified, and delivered a final summary in final.txt.
serial.verification: Ran the local agent test suite to 36/36 pass and reported additional compile/edge checks before final response.
serial.unfinished_or_incorrect: No procedural unfinished state is visible, but official hidden testing still failed parser_accepts_aaa, matching the parallel official failure.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: The parallel run recognized the same 27 lexer and parser requirement slugs and reached 100 percent patch progress by the end of round 2.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: The serial run recognized the same 27 requirements and reported all 27 implemented with zero blocked work in its final response.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Requirement coverage was broadly similar; the material difference is closure and workflow lifecycle, not recognized task scope.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: The parallel parent kept implementation responsibility but also launched design and audit workflows, producing multiple child agents in round 2.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: The serial control used one non-delegating agent path with workflows and delegation tools disabled.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Parallel split advisory and verifier work across child agents while serial performed the implementation and verification sequence locally.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel workflow prompts carried detailed files, requirements, tests, and read-only constraints for advisory/audit children.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial retained the task context in one actor and summarized the implemented lexer and parser entry points in the final response.
comparison_dimensions.difference: There is no proven missing requirement or interface contract in the parallel child briefs; the context issue was result availability after fan-out.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel completed requirement patches by the end of round 2 after parent implementation and additional workflow-backed parser/audit activity.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial implemented lexer and parser changes sequentially and confirmed each requirement patch file was non-empty.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Both produced broad implementations; serial reached a cleaner implementation audit, while parallel was still running audit/design machinery at timeout.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel round 2 shows workflow results were not retrieved without stop, with a protocol failure for stopped or unretrieved workflows.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial had no child result lifecycle and ended with a normal final response after local verification.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Parallel left workflow aggregate results killed/unretrieved, while serial had no delegated results to join and delivered a final answer.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel used a shared workspace while parent edits and children inspected or audited, but status reports no contamination evidence.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial made direct edits in one workspace and reported shipped data/reference files remained unmodified.
comparison_dimensions.difference: No concrete write collision or contamination distinguishes the attempts; integration risk in parallel is dominated by unfinished workflow lifecycle.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel ran local and adversarial checks and launched an exhaustive audit workflow, but the workflow was killed before aggregate completion and official evaluation still failed one parser case.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial reran its local regression suite to 36/36 and returned that evidence, but official evaluation failed the same hidden parser case.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Serial verification was closed and reported; parallel verification was broader but not fully returned before timeout. Neither caught the hidden aaa parser miss.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel round 2 consumed high total and workflow-child budget and ended with agent_timeout after two workflow tasks.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial had zero workflow tasks, zero workflow-child tokens, process_ok true, and failure_mode none for the agent run.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Parallel exhausted closure budget through fan-out and did not produce final.txt, while serial completed just under the per-round window.

outcome_analysis.explanation: The official completed evaluations are not discordant: both parallel and serial have solution_passed=false and both fail test_expanded.py::TestParserSyntacticAnalysis::test_parser_accepts_aaa. The concrete difference is that serial completed cleanly with local 36/36 tests and final delivery, whereas parallel reached 100 percent patch progress but timed out with broad workflow fan-out and unretrieved/killed workflow aggregates. That adverse parallel process difference is real but is not evidenced as the cause of the shared hidden parser failure.
parallel_contributors: agent_timeout after broad design/audit workflow fan-out
workflow aggregate results killed or unretrieved before final closure
serial_contributors: local test suite reported 36/36 pass and final response recorded 27/27 requirements
ordinary_implementation_differences: Both final solutions missed the hidden parser_accepts_aaa behavior, so the official failure is best treated as a shared ordinary implementation/evaluator-aligned defect rather than a parallel-only coordination consequence.
evaluator_effects: Current cell/status.json evaluation supersedes stale aggregates; passed/total/rate are unavailable in resolver fields, but per-test maps identify the shared failing hidden case.
outcome_analysis.causal_scope: no official outcome difference; retained label describes adverse parallel process consequence only

The workflow state files themselves ended killed with null aggregate results, so the fan-out consumed closure budget and left verifier/design synthesis unavailable.

candidates.near_match_reason: Missing verifier return is visible as a terminal symptom, but the directly evidenced boundary is the collective fan-out and budget exhaustion that killed/nullified the workflow results.
